#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum ParseError {
    /// A fully formatted error message.
    Msg(String),
}

impl std::fmt::Display for ParseError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            ParseError::Msg(m) => write!(f, "{}", m),
        }
    }
}

fn err<T>(msg: String) -> Result<T, ParseError> {
    Err(ParseError::Msg(msg))
}

struct Lookup {
    def: &'static FlagDef,
    negated: bool,
}

fn find_long(name: &str) -> Option<Lookup> {
    for def in FLAGS.iter() {
        if def.long == name || def.aliases.iter().any(|a| *a == name) {
            return Some(Lookup { def, negated: false });
        }
        if def.negated == Some(name) {
            return Some(Lookup { def, negated: true });
        }
    }
    None
}

fn find_short(c: u8) -> Option<&'static FlagDef> {
    FLAGS.iter().find(|d| d.short == Some(c))
}

fn ngrams(s: &str) -> std::collections::BTreeSet<String> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = s.chars().collect();
    let mut set = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
    if chars.len() < 3 {
        // fall back to the whole string
        set.insert(s.to_string());
        return set;
    }
    for w in chars.windows(3) {
        set.insert(w.iter().collect());
    }
    set
}

fn similar_flags(name: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let given = ngrams(name);
    let mut out = vec![];
    let mut check = |cand: &str, out: &mut Vec<String>| {
        let other = ngrams(cand);
        let inter = given.intersection(&other).count() as f64;
        let union = given.union(&other).count() as f64;
        if union > 0.0 && inter / union >= 0.4 {
            out.push(format!("--{}", cand));
        }
    };
    for def in FLAGS.iter() {
        check(def.long, &mut out);
        for a in def.aliases {
            check(a, &mut out);
        }
        if let Some(n) = def.negated {
            check(n, &mut out);
        }
    }
    out
}

fn unrecognized_long(name: &str) -> ParseError {
    let mut msg = format!("unrecognized flag --{}", name);
    let similar = similar_flags(name);
    if !similar.is_empty() {
        msg.push_str("\n\nsimilar flags that are available: ");
        msg.push_str(&similar.join(", "));
    }
    ParseError::Msg(msg)
}

/// Parse the given arguments (not including the binary name) into the given
/// low args value.
pub fn parse(args: Vec<OsString>, low: &mut LowArgs) -> Result<(), ParseError> {
    let mut i = 0;
    let mut only_positional = false;
    while i < args.len() {
        let arg = &args[i];
        i += 1;
        if only_positional {
            low.positional.push(arg.clone());
            continue;
        }
        let bytes = os_bytes(arg);
        if bytes == b"--" {
            only_positional = true;
            continue;
        }
        if bytes.starts_with(b"--") {
            let rest = &bytes[2..];
            let (name_b, inline) = match rest.iter().position(|&b| b == b'=') {
                Some(p) => (&rest[..p], Some(bytes_to_os(&rest[p + 1..]))),
                None => (rest, None),
            };
            let name = String::from_utf8_lossy(name_b).into_owned();
            let display = format!("--{}", name);
            let lk = match find_long(&name) {
                Some(lk) => lk,
                None => return Err(unrecognized_long(&name)),
            };
            if lk.def.switch || lk.negated {
                if let Some(v) = inline {
                    return err(format!(
                        "invalid CLI arguments: unexpected argument for option '{}': {:?}",
                        display,
                        v.to_string_lossy()
                    ));
                }
                apply(low, lk.def.flag, &display, lk.negated, None)?;
            } else {
                let value = match inline {
                    Some(v) => v,
                    None => {
                        if i < args.len() {
                            i += 1;
                            args[i - 1].clone()
                        } else {
                            return err(format!(
                                "missing value for flag {}: missing argument for option '{}'",
                                display, display
                            ));
                        }
                    }
                };
                apply(low, lk.def.flag, &display, false, Some(value))?;
            }
            continue;
        }
        if bytes.len() > 1 && bytes[0] == b'-' {
            let mut j = 1;
            while j < bytes.len() {
                let c = bytes[j];
                // Decode a full character for error reporting.
                let display = {
                    let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(&bytes[j..]);
                    let ch = s.chars().next().unwrap_or('?');
                    format!("-{}", ch)
                };
                let def = match find_short(c) {
                    Some(d) if c.is_ascii() => d,
                    _ => {
                        return err(format!("unrecognized flag {}", display));
                    }
                };
                j += 1;
                if def.switch {
                    if j < bytes.len() && bytes[j] == b'=' {
                        let v = bytes_to_os(&bytes[j + 1..]);
                        return err(format!(
                            "invalid CLI arguments: unexpected argument for option '{}': {:?}",
                            display,
                            v.to_string_lossy()
                        ));
                    }
                    apply(low, def.flag, &display, false, None)?;
                } else {
                    let value = if j < bytes.len() {
                        let mut start = j;
                        if bytes[start] == b'=' {
                            start += 1;
                        }
                        bytes_to_os(&bytes[start..])
                    } else if i < args.len() {
                        i += 1;
                        args[i - 1].clone()
                    } else {
                        return err(format!(
                            "missing value for flag {}: missing argument for option '{}'",
                            display, display
                        ));
                    };
                    apply(low, def.flag, &display, false, Some(value))?;
                    break;
                }
            }
            continue;
        }
        low.positional.push(arg.clone());
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub fn os_bytes(s: &OsStr) -> &[u8] {
    use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
    s.as_bytes()
}

pub fn bytes_to_os(b: &[u8]) -> OsString {
    use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
    OsStr::from_bytes(b).to_os_string()
}

fn value_str(name: &str, v: &OsString) -> Result<String, ParseError> {
    match v.to_str() {
        Some(s) => Ok(s.to_string()),
        None => err(format!(
            "error parsing flag {}: value is not valid UTF-8",
            name
        )),
    }
}

fn parse_number<T: std::str::FromStr>(name: &str, v: &OsString) -> Result<T, ParseError>
where
    T::Err: std::fmt::Display,
{
    let s = value_str(name, v)?;
    match s.parse::<T>() {
        Ok(n) => Ok(n),
        Err(e) => err(format!("error parsing flag {}: value is not a valid number: {}", name, e)),
    }
}

fn parse_size(name: &str, v: &OsString) -> Result<u64, ParseError> {
    let s = value_str(name, v)?;
    let fmt_err = || {
        err(format!(
            "error parsing flag {}: invalid size: invalid format for size '{}', which should be a non-empty sequence of digits followed by an optional 'K', 'M' or 'G' suffix",
            name, s
        ))
    };
    let (digits, mult): (&str, u64) = if let Some(d) = s.strip_suffix('K') {
        (d, 1 << 10)
    } else if let Some(d) = s.strip_suffix('M') {
        (d, 1 << 20)
    } else if let Some(d) = s.strip_suffix('G') {
        (d, 1 << 30)
    } else {
        (&s[..], 1)
    };
    if digits.is_empty() || !digits.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_digit()) {
        return fmt_err();
    }
    let n: u64 = match digits.parse() {
        Ok(n) => n,
        Err(e) => {
            return err(format!(
                "error parsing flag {}: invalid size: invalid integer found in size '{}': {}",
                name, s, e
            ))
        }
    };
    match n.checked_mul(mult) {
        Some(n) => Ok(n),
        None => err(format!("error parsing flag {}: invalid size: size too big in '{}'", name, s)),
    }
}

fn choice_err<T>(name: &str, v: &str) -> Result<T, ParseError> {
    err(format!("error parsing flag {}: choice '{}' is unrecognized", name, v))
}

fn apply(
    low: &mut LowArgs,
    flag: F,
    name: &str,
    negated: bool,
    value: Option<OsString>,
) -> Result<(), ParseError> {
    let v = value.unwrap_or_default();
    match flag {
        F::Regexp => {
            let s = value_str(name, &v)?;
            low.patterns.push(PatternSource::Regexp(s));
        }
        F::File => {
            low.patterns.push(PatternSource::File(PathBuf::from(v)));
        }
        F::AfterContext => {
            let n = parse_number::<usize>(name, &v)?;
            low.context.set_after(n);
        }
        F::BeforeContext => {
            let n = parse_number::<usize>(name, &v)?;
            low.context.set_before(n);
        }
        F::Context => {
            let n = parse_number::<usize>(name, &v)?;
            low.context.set_both(n);
        }
        F::Binary => {
            low.binary = if negated { BinaryMode::Auto } else { BinaryMode::SearchAndSuppress };
        }
        F::BlockBuffered => {
            low.buffer = if negated { BufferMode::Auto } else { BufferMode::Block };
        }
        F::LineBuffered => {
            low.buffer = if negated { BufferMode::Auto } else { BufferMode::Line };
        }
        F::ByteOffset => low.byte_offset = !negated,
        F::CaseSensitive => low.case = CaseMode::Sensitive,
        F::IgnoreCase => low.case = CaseMode::Insensitive,
        F::SmartCase => low.case = CaseMode::Smart,
        F::Color => {
            let s = value_str(name, &v)?;
            low.color = match &*s {
                "never" => ColorChoice::Never,
                "auto" => ColorChoice::Auto,
                "always" => ColorChoice::Always,
                "ansi" => ColorChoice::Ansi,
                _ => return choice_err(name, &s),
            };
        }
        F::Colors => {
            let s = value_str(name, &v)?;
            match crate::color::UserColorSpec::parse(&s) {
                Ok(spec) => low.colors.push(spec),
                Err(e) => return err(format!("error parsing flag {}: {}", name, e)),
            }
        }
        F::Column => low.column = Some(!negated),
        F::ContextSeparator => {
            if negated {
                low.context_separator = None;
            } else {
                low.context_separator = Some(crate::util::unescape_os(&v));
            }
        }
        F::Count => low.mode = Mode::Search(SearchMode::Count),
        F::CountMatches => low.mode = Mode::Search(SearchMode::CountMatches),
        F::FilesWithMatches => low.mode = Mode::Search(SearchMode::FilesWithMatches),
        F::FilesWithoutMatch => low.mode = Mode::Search(SearchMode::FilesWithoutMatch),
        F::Json => {
            if negated {
                if low.mode == Mode::Search(SearchMode::JSON) {
                    low.mode = Mode::Search(SearchMode::Standard);
                }
            } else {
                low.mode = Mode::Search(SearchMode::JSON);
            }
        }
        F::Files => low.mode = Mode::Files,
        F::TypeList => low.mode = Mode::Types,
        F::Generate => {
            let s = value_str(name, &v)?;
            let g = match &*s {
                "man" => GenerateMode::Man,
                "complete-bash" => GenerateMode::CompleteBash,
                "complete-zsh" => GenerateMode::CompleteZsh,
                "complete-fish" => GenerateMode::CompleteFish,
                "complete-powershell" => GenerateMode::CompletePowerShell,
                _ => return choice_err(name, &s),
            };
            low.mode = Mode::Generate(g);
        }
        F::Crlf => {
            if negated {
                low.crlf = false;
            } else {
                low.crlf = true;
                low.null_data = false;
            }
        }
        F::NullData => {
            low.null_data = true;
            low.crlf = false;
        }
        F::Debug => low.logging = Some(LoggingMode::Debug),
        F::Trace => low.logging = Some(LoggingMode::Trace),
        F::DfaSizeLimit => {
            let n = parse_size(name, &v)?;
            low.dfa_size_limit = Some(usize::try_from(n).unwrap_or(usize::MAX));
        }
        F::RegexSizeLimit => {
            let n = parse_size(name, &v)?;
            low.regex_size_limit = Some(usize::try_from(n).unwrap_or(usize::MAX));
        }
        F::MaxFilesize => {
            let n = parse_size(name, &v)?;
            low.max_filesize = Some(n);
        }
        F::Encoding => {
            if negated {
                low.encoding = EncodingMode::Auto;
            } else {
                let s = value_str(name, &v)?;
                let lower = s.to_ascii_lowercase();
                if lower == "auto" {
                    low.encoding = EncodingMode::Auto;
                } else if lower == "none" {
                    low.encoding = EncodingMode::Disabled;
                } else {
                    match crate::encoding::Encoding::for_label(s.as_bytes()) {
                        Some(_) => low.encoding = EncodingMode::Some(s),
                        None => {
                            return err(format!(
                                "error parsing flag {}: grep config error: unknown encoding: {}",
                                name, s
                            ))
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        F::Engine => {
            let s = value_str(name, &v)?;
            low.engine = match &*s {
                "default" => EngineChoice::Default,
                "pcre2" => EngineChoice::PCRE2,
                "auto" => EngineChoice::Auto,
                _ => return choice_err(name, &s),
            };
        }
        F::Pcre2 => {
            low.engine = if negated { EngineChoice::Default } else { EngineChoice::PCRE2 };
        }
        F::AutoHybridRegex => {
            low.engine = if negated { EngineChoice::Default } else { EngineChoice::Auto };
        }
        F::FieldContextSeparator => {
            low.field_context_separator = crate::util::unescape_os(&v);
        }
        F::FieldMatchSeparator => {
            low.field_match_separator = crate::util::unescape_os(&v);
        }
        F::FixedStrings => low.fixed_strings = !negated,
        F::Follow => low.follow = !negated,
        F::Glob => {
            let s = value_str(name, &v)?;
            low.globs.push(s);
        }
        F::IGlob => {
            let s = value_str(name, &v)?;
            low.iglobs.push(s);
        }
        F::GlobCaseInsensitive => low.glob_case_insensitive = !negated,
        F::Heading => low.heading = Some(!negated),
        F::Help => {
            low.special = Some(if name == "-h" { SpecialMode::HelpShort } else { SpecialMode::HelpLong });
        }
        F::Version => {
            low.special =
                Some(if name == "-V" { SpecialMode::VersionShort } else { SpecialMode::VersionLong });
        }
        F::Pcre2Version => low.special = Some(SpecialMode::VersionPCRE2),
        F::Hidden => low.hidden = !negated,
        F::HostnameBin => {
            low.hostname_bin = Some(PathBuf::from(v));
        }
        F::HyperlinkFormat => {
            let s = value_str(name, &v)?;
            if let Err(e) = crate::hyperlink::HyperlinkFormat::parse(&s) {
                return err(format!("error parsing flag {}: {}", name, e));
            }
            low.hyperlink_format = s;
        }
        F::IgnoreFile => low.ignore_file.push(PathBuf::from(v)),
        F::IgnoreFileCaseInsensitive => low.ignore_file_case_insensitive = !negated,
        F::IncludeZero => low.include_zero = !negated,
        F::InvertMatch => low.invert_match = !negated,
        F::LineNumber => low.line_number = Some(true),
        F::LineNumberNo => low.line_number = Some(false),
        F::LineRegexp => low.boundary = Some(BoundaryMode::Line),
        F::WordRegexp => low.boundary = Some(BoundaryMode::Word),
        F::MaxColumns => {
            let n = parse_number::<u64>(name, &v)?;
            low.max_columns = if n == 0 { None } else { Some(n) };
        }
        F::MaxColumnsPreview => low.max_columns_preview = !negated,
        F::MaxCount => {
            let n = parse_number::<u64>(name, &v)?;
            low.max_count = Some(n);
        }
        F::MaxDepth => {
            let n = parse_number::<usize>(name, &v)?;
            low.max_depth = Some(n);
        }
        F::Mmap => {
            low.mmap = if negated { MmapMode::Never } else { MmapMode::AlwaysTryMmap };
        }
        F::Multiline => {
            low.multiline = !negated;
            if !negated {
                low.stop_on_nonmatch = false;
            }
        }
        F::MultilineDotall => low.multiline_dotall = !negated,
        F::NoConfig => low.no_config = true,
        F::NoIgnore => {
            let yes = !negated;
            low.no_ignore_dot = yes;
            low.no_ignore_exclude = yes;
            low.no_ignore_global = yes;
            low.no_ignore_parent = yes;
            low.no_ignore_vcs = yes;
        }
        F::NoIgnoreDot => low.no_ignore_dot = !negated,
        F::NoIgnoreExclude => low.no_ignore_exclude = !negated,
        F::NoIgnoreFiles => low.no_ignore_files = !negated,
        F::NoIgnoreGlobal => low.no_ignore_global = !negated,
        F::NoIgnoreMessages => low.no_ignore_messages = !negated,
        F::NoIgnoreParent => low.no_ignore_parent = !negated,
        F::NoIgnoreVcs => low.no_ignore_vcs = !negated,
        F::NoMessages => low.no_messages = !negated,
        F::NoRequireGit => low.no_require_git = !negated,
        F::NoUnicode => low.no_unicode = !negated,
        F::NoPcre2Unicode => low.no_unicode = !negated,
        F::Null => low.null = true,
        F::OneFileSystem => low.one_file_system = !negated,
        F::OnlyMatching => low.only_matching = true,
        F::PathSeparator => {
            let sep = crate::util::unescape_os(&v);
            if sep.is_empty() {
                low.path_separator = None;
            } else if sep.len() > 1 {
                return err(format!(
                    "error parsing flag {}: A path separator must be exactly one byte, but the given separator is {} bytes: {}\nIn some shells on Windows '/' is automatically expanded. Use '//' instead.",
                    name,
                    sep.len(),
                    String::from_utf8_lossy(&sep)
                ));
            } else {
                low.path_separator = Some(sep[0]);
            }
        }
        F::Passthru => low.context = ContextMode::Passthru,
        F::Pre => {
            if negated {
                low.pre = None;
            } else {
                if v.is_empty() {
                    low.pre = None;
                } else {
                    low.pre = Some(PathBuf::from(v));
                    low.search_zip = false;
                }
            }
        }
        F::PreGlob => {
            let s = value_str(name, &v)?;
            low.pre_glob.push(s);
        }
        F::Pretty => {
            low.color = ColorChoice::Always;
            low.heading = Some(true);
            low.line_number = Some(true);
        }
        F::Quiet => low.quiet = true,
        F::Replace => {
            low.replace = Some(os_bytes(&v).to_vec());
        }
        F::SearchZip => {
            if negated {
                low.search_zip = false;
            } else {
                low.search_zip = true;
                low.pre = None;
            }
        }
        F::Sort | F::Sortr => {
            let s = value_str(name, &v)?;
            let kind = match &*s {
                "none" => None,
                "path" => Some(SortModeKind::Path),
                "modified" => Some(SortModeKind::LastModified),
                "accessed" => Some(SortModeKind::LastAccessed),
                "created" => Some(SortModeKind::Created),
                _ => return choice_err(name, &s),
            };
            low.sort = kind.map(|kind| SortMode { reverse: flag == F::Sortr, kind });
        }
        F::SortFiles => {
            if negated {
                low.sort = None;
            } else {
                low.sort = Some(SortMode { reverse: false, kind: SortModeKind::Path });
            }
        }
        F::Stats => low.stats = !negated,
        F::StopOnNonmatch => {
            low.stop_on_nonmatch = true;
            low.multiline = false;
        }
        F::Text => {
            low.binary = if negated { BinaryMode::Auto } else { BinaryMode::AsText };
        }
        F::Threads => {
            let n = parse_number::<usize>(name, &v)?;
            low.threads = if n == 0 { None } else { Some(n) };
        }
        F::Trim => low.trim = !negated,
        F::Type => {
            let s = value_str(name, &v)?;
            low.type_changes.push(TypeChange::Select { name: s });
        }
        F::TypeNot => {
            let s = value_str(name, &v)?;
            low.type_changes.push(TypeChange::Negate { name: s });
        }
        F::TypeAdd => {
            let s = value_str(name, &v)?;
            low.type_changes.push(TypeChange::Add { def: s });
        }
        F::TypeClear => {
            let s = value_str(name, &v)?;
            low.type_changes.push(TypeChange::Clear { name: s });
        }
        F::Unrestricted => {
            low.unrestricted += 1;
            if low.unrestricted == 1 {
                low.no_ignore_dot = true;
                low.no_ignore_exclude = true;
                low.no_ignore_global = true;
                low.no_ignore_parent = true;
                low.no_ignore_vcs = true;
            } else if low.unrestricted == 2 {
                low.hidden = true;
            } else if low.unrestricted == 3 {
                low.binary = BinaryMode::AsText;
                low.binary = BinaryMode::SearchAndSuppress;
            }
        }
        F::Vimgrep => low.vimgrep = true,
        F::WithFilename => low.with_filename = Some(true),
        F::WithFilenameNo => low.with_filename = Some(false),
    }
    Ok(())
}

# Generates single byte encoding tables for src/encoding_tables.rs
import codecs
encs = [
    ("IBM866", "cp866", False),
    ("ISO_8859_2", "iso8859_2", False),
    ("ISO_8859_3", "iso8859_3", False),
    ("ISO_8859_4", "iso8859_4", False),
    ("ISO_8859_5", "iso8859_5", False),
    ("ISO_8859_6", "iso8859_6", False),
    ("ISO_8859_7", "iso8859_7", False),
    ("ISO_8859_8", "iso8859_8", False),
    ("ISO_8859_10", "iso8859_10", False),
    ("ISO_8859_13", "iso8859_13", False),
    ("ISO_8859_14", "iso8859_14", False),
    ("ISO_8859_15", "iso8859_15", False),
    ("ISO_8859_16", "iso8859_16", False),
    ("KOI8_R", "koi8_r", False),
    ("KOI8_U", "koi8_u", False),
    ("MACINTOSH", "mac_roman", False),
    ("WINDOWS_874", "cp874", True),
    ("WINDOWS_1250", "cp1250", True),
    ("WINDOWS_1251", "cp1251", True),
    ("WINDOWS_1252", "cp1252", True),
    ("WINDOWS_1253", "cp1253", True),
    ("WINDOWS_1254", "cp1254", True),
    ("WINDOWS_1255", "cp1255", True),
    ("WINDOWS_1256", "cp1256", True),
    ("WINDOWS_1257", "cp1257", True),
    ("WINDOWS_1258", "cp1258", True),
    ("X_MAC_CYRILLIC", "mac_cyrillic", False),
]
out = ["// Generated by tools/gen_sbcs.py. Upper half (0x80..0xFF) of single byte encodings.", ""]
for name, py, win in encs:
    vals = []
    for b in range(0x80, 0x100):
        try:
            s = bytes([b]).decode(py)
            assert len(s) == 1
            vals.append(ord(s))
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            if win and b < 0xA0:
                vals.append(b)
            else:
                vals.append(0xFFFD)
    if name == "KOI8_U":
        vals[0xAE - 0x80] = 0x045E
        vals[0xBE - 0x80] = 0x040E
    out.append("pub static %s: [u16; 128] = [" % name)
    for i in range(0, 128, 8):
        out.append("    " + ", ".join("0x%04X" % v for v in vals[i:i+8]) + ",")
    out.append("];")
    out.append("")
open("/workspace/src/encoding_tables.rs", "w").write("\n".join(out))
EOF
python3 /workspace/tools/gen_sbcs.py && wc -l /workspace/src/encoding_tables.rs

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Differential tester: runs commands against the reference rg and ours."""
import subprocess, sys, os, shlex

REF = os.environ.get("REF", "/tmp/ref/rg_orig")
OURS = os.environ.get("OURS", "/workspace/executable")

def run(binary, args, cwd, stdin, env):
    e = dict(os.environ)
    e.update(env or {})
    p = subprocess.run([binary] + args, cwd=cwd, input=stdin, capture_output=True, env=e, timeout=30)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr

def main():
    path = sys.argv[1]
    verbose = "-v" in sys.argv
    cases = []
    cwd = "/tmp"
    for line in open(path):
        line = line.rstrip("\n")
        if not line.strip() or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        if line.startswith("cd "):
            cwd = line[3:].strip()
            continue
        stdin = None
        if " <<< " in line:
            line, s = line.split(" <<< ", 1)
            stdin = s.encode().decode("unicode_escape").encode("latin1")
        cases.append((cwd, line, stdin))
    fails = 0
    order_only = 0
    for cwd, line, stdin in cases:
        args = shlex.split(line)
        env = {}
        while args and "=" in args[0] and not args[0].startswith("-"):
            k, v = args.pop(0).split("=", 1)
            env[k] = v
        if stdin is None:
            stdin_arg = b""
        else:
            stdin_arg = stdin
        r = run(REF, args, cwd, stdin_arg if stdin is not None else None, env) if stdin is not None else run_devnull(REF, args, cwd, env)
        o = run(OURS, args, cwd, stdin_arg if stdin is not None else None, env) if stdin is not None else run_devnull(OURS, args, cwd, env)
        if r == o:
            continue
        if r[0] == o[0] and sorted(r[1].split(b"\n")) == sorted(o[1].split(b"\n")) and sorted(r[2].split(b"\n")) == sorted(o[2].split(b"\n")):
            order_only += 1
            if verbose:
                print("ORDER-ONLY: [%s] %s" % (cwd, line))
            continue
        fails += 1
        print("=" * 70)
        print("FAIL: [%s] %s" % (cwd, line))
        if r[0] != o[0]:
            print("  exit: ref=%d ours=%d" % (r[0], o[0]))
        if r[1] != o[1]:
            print("  stdout ref:\n" + indent(r[1]))
            print("  stdout ours:\n" + indent(o[1]))
        if r[2] != o[2]:
            print("  stderr ref:\n" + indent(r[2]))
            print("  stderr ours:\n" + indent(o[2]))
    print("total=%d fail=%d order_only=%d" % (len(cases), fails, order_only))

def run_devnull(binary, args, cwd, env):
    e = dict(os.environ)
    e.update(env or {})
    with open(os.devnull, "rb") as dn:
        p = subprocess.run([binary] + args, cwd=cwd, stdin=dn, capture_output=True, env=e, timeout=30)
    return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr

def indent(b):
    s = b.decode("utf-8", "replace")
    lines = s.split("\n")
    if len(lines) > 40:
        lines = lines[:40] + ["... (%d more lines)" % (len(lines) - 40)]
    return "\n".join("    | " + l for l in lines)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF

# Generates CJK decoding tables (binary, little-endian u32 per pointer, 0 = unmapped)
import struct, os
out = "/workspace/src/tables"
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)

def dec(b, codec):
    try:
        s = b.decode(codec)
        if len(s) == 1:
            return ord(s)
        return 0
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        return 0

def write(name, vals):
    with open(os.path.join(out, name), "wb") as f:
        for v in vals:
            f.write(struct.pack("<I", v))

# jis0208 via Shift_JIS (cp932) pointers 0..11279
vals = []
for p in range(11280):
    lead = p // 188
    trail = p % 188
    lb = lead + (0x81 if lead < 0x1F else 0xC1)
    tb = trail + (0x40 if trail < 0x3F else 0x41)
    if lb > 0xFC:
        vals.append(0); continue
    v = dec(bytes([lb, tb]), "cp932")
    vals.append(v)
write("jis0208.bin", vals)

# jis0212 via euc_jp 0x8F prefix, pointers 0..8835
vals = []
for p in range(94 * 94):
    l = p // 94 + 0xA1
    b = p % 94 + 0xA1
    vals.append(dec(bytes([0x8F, l, b]), "euc_jp"))
write("jis0212.bin", vals)

# euc-kr via cp949, pointers (lead-0x81)*190 + (byte-0x41)
vals = []
for p in range(126 * 190):
    l = p // 190 + 0x81
    b = p % 190 + 0x41
    vals.append(dec(bytes([l, b]), "cp949"))
write("euckr.bin", vals)

# big5 via big5hkscs, pointers (lead-0x81)*157 + (byte-offset)
vals = []
for p in range(126 * 157):
    l = p // 157 + 0x81
    t = p % 157
    b = t + (0x40 if t < 0x3F else 0x62)
    vals.append(dec(bytes([l, b]), "big5hkscs"))
write("big5.bin", vals)

# gb18030 two byte, pointers (lead-0x81)*190 + (byte - offset)
vals = []
for p in range(126 * 190):
    l = p // 190 + 0x81
    t = p % 190
    b = t + (0x40 if t < 0x3F else 0x41)
    vals.append(dec(bytes([l, b]), "gb18030"))
write("gb18030.bin", vals)

# gb18030 four byte ranges for BMP: pointer -> code point
ranges = []
prev = None
for p in range(39420):
    b1 = p // 12600 + 0x81
    r = p % 12600
    b2 = r // 1260 + 0x30
    r = r % 1260
    b3 = r // 10 + 0x81
    b4 = r % 10 + 0x30
    cp = dec(bytes([b1, b2, b3, b4]), "gb18030")
    if cp == 0:
        prev = None
        continue
    if prev is not None and cp - p == prev:
        continue
    ranges.append((p, cp))
    prev = cp - p
with open(os.path.join(out, "gb18030_ranges.bin"), "wb") as f:
    for p, cp in ranges:
        f.write(struct.pack("<II", p, cp))
print(len(ranges), "ranges")

    let ch = char::from_u32(c).unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}');
    let mut buf = [0u8; 4];
    out.extend_from_slice(ch.encode_utf8(&mut buf).as_bytes());
}

/// Decode UTF-8 with replacement of invalid sequences, following the WHATWG
/// "maximal subpart" replacement strategy (which is what Rust's lossy
/// conversion does too).
fn decode_utf8(input: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
    let s = String::from_utf8_lossy(input);
    out.extend_from_slice(s.as_bytes());
}

fn decode_utf16(input: &[u8], be: bool, out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
    let mut i = 0;
    let mut pending_lead: Option<u16> = None;
    while i + 1 < input.len() {
        let u = if be {
            u16::from_be_bytes([input[i], input[i + 1]])
        } else {
            u16::from_le_bytes([input[i], input[i + 1]])
        };
        i += 2;
        if let Some(lead) = pending_lead.take() {
            if (0xDC00..0xE000).contains(&u) {
                let c = 0x10000 + (((lead as u32) - 0xD800) << 10) + ((u as u32) - 0xDC00);
                push_char(out, c);
                continue;
            } else {
                push_char(out, 0xFFFD);
            }
        }
        if (0xD800..0xDC00).contains(&u) {
            pending_lead = Some(u);
        } else if (0xDC00..0xE000).contains(&u) {
            push_char(out, 0xFFFD);
        } else {
            push_char(out, u as u32);
        }
    }
    if pending_lead.is_some() {
        push_char(out, 0xFFFD);
    }
    if i < input.len() {
        push_char(out, 0xFFFD);
    }
}

/// Decode the given bytes using the given encoding, producing UTF-8.
pub fn decode(enc: Encoding, input: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(input.len());
    match enc {
        Encoding::Utf8 => decode_utf8(input, &mut out),
        Encoding::Utf16Le => decode_utf16(input, false, &mut out),
        Encoding::Utf16Be => decode_utf16(input, true, &mut out),
        Encoding::UserDefined => {
            for &b in input {
                if b < 0x80 {
                    out.push(b);
                } else {
                    push_char(&mut out, 0xF780 + (b as u32 - 0x80));
                }
            }
        }
        Encoding::Single(table, _) => {
            for &b in input {
                if b < 0x80 {
                    out.push(b);
                } else {
                    push_char(&mut out, table[(b - 0x80) as usize] as u32);
                }
            }
        }
        Encoding::Multi(name) => crate::encoding_cjk::decode(name, input, &mut out),
    }
    out
}

/// Apply ripgrep's BOM sniffing and transcoding rules. Returns None when the
/// data should be searched as is.
pub fn transcode(explicit: Option<Encoding>, data: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    if data.starts_with(&[0xFF, 0xFE]) {
        return Some(decode(Encoding::Utf16Le, &data[2..]));
    }
    if data.starts_with(&[0xFE, 0xFF]) {
        return Some(decode(Encoding::Utf16Be, &data[2..]));
    }
    let (bom, rest) = if data.starts_with(&[0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF]) {
        (true, &data[3..])
    } else {
        (false, data)
    };
    match explicit {
        None => {
            if bom {
                Some(rest.to_vec())
            } else {
                None
            }
        }
        Some(enc) => Some(decode(enc, rest)),
    }
}

I've written a Rust reimplementation of `./executable`, which is ripgrep 14.1.1. On every deterministic case I compared against the original, the output and exit codes match. Everything is committed, and `./compile.sh` builds a fresh clone offline and writes `./executable`. Build outputs (`target/` and `executable`) are in `.gitignore`.

**Dependencies and the build:** I used general-purpose crates from the local cargo cache (`regex-automata`, `regex-syntax`, `memchr`, `bstr`, `libc`). I deliberately did not use `globset` or `ignore`: they were in the cache, but they come from the ripgrep project itself. The build assumes the grading environment has the same local crate cache, because there's no network. If it doesn't, `compile.sh` falls back to an online build, which would fail.

**How I checked it:** I renamed the original binary (moving it to `/tmp/ref/rg_orig`) so `compile.sh` wouldn't overwrite it, then compared the two directly. The comparisons that came back clean:
- 23 hand-written case lists, about 1,000 commands, kept in `tests/cases*.txt`.
- Randomised runs, many thousands in all, covering:
  - general flag and pattern combinations on fixture files;
  - random bytes;
  - piped stdin;
  - random `.gitignore` trees;
  - random globs;
  - random flag and value combinations.

`tools/difftest.py`, `tools/fuzz.py` and `tools/mkfixtures.sh` are committed and expect the original at `/tmp/ref/rg_orig`. The other fuzzers were throwaway scripts in `/tmp` and aren't in the repo.

**Where it can still differ:**
- **Output order with several threads.** The original's file order varies from run to run when it searches in parallel. I always print in its most common order. Tests that use `--sort`, `-j1` or a single file are deterministic.
- **`--debug` / `--trace`.** These print nothing extra. The original's messages include source file paths, the hostname and the thread count, so they couldn't match exactly anyway.
- **One rare encoding case.** With an explicit encoding plus `-U`, the original sometimes drops part of a trailing replacement character; I don't reproduce that.
- **Help, man page and completions.** These are embedded as captured text rather than generated.

**Behaviours copied deliberately.** Several are odd but are what the original actually does:
- How the internal read buffer splits files into chunks, which decides when a file is detected as binary.
- Some quirks in how `.gitignore` files in parent directories are applied.
- `--count-matches -v` counts lines rather than matches.
- How file separators are written differs between single- and multi-threaded runs.

**Other details matched:**
- Error messages and the order they appear in.
- "Similar flags" suggestions for unknown flags.
- Colours and hyperlinks.
- JSON output.
- Shift_JIS, EUC-JP and the other CJK encodings.
- `--pre` and `-z`.
- Reading stdin as a stream, so `yes | rg -m1 y` exits instead of hanging.

- **One rare encoding case.** With an explicit encoding plus `-U`, the original sometimes drops part of a trailing replacement character; I don't reproduce that.
- **Help, man page and completions.** These are embedded as captured text rather than generated.

**Behaviours copied deliberately.** Several are odd but are what the original actually does:
- How the internal read buffer splits files into chunks, which decides when a file is detected as binary.
- Some quirks in how `.gitignore` files in parent directories are applied.
- `--count-matches -v` counts lines rather than matches.
- How file separators are written differs between single- and multi-threaded runs.

**Other details matched:**
- Error messages and the order they appear in.
- "Similar flags" suggestions for unknown flags.
- Colours and hyperlinks.
- JSON output.
- Shift_JIS, EUC-JP and the other CJK encodings.
- `--pre` and `-z`.
- Reading stdin as a stream, so `yes | rg -m1 y` exits instead of hanging.

content.text:
I've written a Rust reimplementation of ripgrep 14.1.1 in `/workspace`. It's committed with a clean working tree, and `./compile.sh` builds `./executable` from a fresh clone. I compared it against the original binary with my own differential tests, and they now pass. Where the original's output order varies from run to run, ours matches its most common order.

**How it was tested:** about 20 hand-written case files covering the main features, plus several random fuzzers run against the original. The fuzzers vary flag combinations, regex patterns, random file contents, stdin input, `.gitignore`/`.ignore` trees and glob patterns, and had covered over 10,000 random cases by the end. I learned the behaviour only by running the original and reading the bundled docs.

**What it covers:**
- **Search:** the regex rules and error messages, every output mode (normal, counts, file lists, quiet, JSON, vimgrep, `--stats`), context lines, colours and hyperlinks.
- **File filtering:** `.gitignore`, `.ignore` and `.rgignore` handling (including parent directories and git's exclude and global ignore files), `-g`/`--iglob` globs, file types and hidden files.
- **Binary and encoding handling:** binary-file detection as the original does it (including its 64 KB read chunks), text encodings including the Japanese, Chinese and Korean ones, and BOM detection.
- **Other options:** compressed-file search (`-z`), `--pre`, the config file, sorting, and the original's exit codes.
- **Help and generated text:** `--help`, `-h`, `--version`, the man page and the shell completions are stored as fixed text copied from the original's output.

**Known gaps:**
- **`--debug` / `--trace`** print nothing extra. The original's debug lines include the hostname and the machine's thread count, so they couldn't match anyway.
- **Output order without `--sort` or `-j1`** follows a fixed order that matches the original's most common one. The original runs multi-threaded, so its own order changes between runs when several files or folders are searched.
- **`-U` on a re-encoded file** (UTF-16 or an explicit `-E` encoding) can differ from the original in its last byte in one rare case.

**Build dependency:** the build uses a few general-purpose crates (`regex-automata`, `regex-syntax`, `memchr`, `bstr`, `libc`) taken offline from the Cargo cache already on this machine. If the grading machine lacks that cache and has no network, the build fails. I did not use the `globset` or `ignore` crates, which are part of ripgrep itself.

The repo also contains my test cases (`tests/`) and helper scripts (`tools/`). The test runners expect the original binary at `/tmp/ref/rg_orig`. I moved it there from `./executable` because `compile.sh` writes over that path.
